newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Gresik says H1 net not encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Gresik says H1 net not encouraging.

text.p: Indonesian cement giant PT Semen Gresik said on Thursday sales during the first half of 1997 were higher against the same period last year but added that net profits during the year were not encouraging.
Gresik said in a statement it sold 5.01 million tonnes during the first half of 1997, or up 15.4 percent from 4.3 million tonnes in the same period of last year.

The first half 1996 volume included pre-commercial sales of 188,263 tonnes of cement from the Tonasa IV plant, while the first half 1997 sales included pre-commercial sales of 365,446 tonnes of cement from Tuban II plant, it said.

Investor relations manager Koestoro said the firm sold 4.65 million tonnes in the first half of 1997, or up 11.8 percent against 4.16 million tonnes in the same period of last year, if the pre-commercial sales were not included.
"Total sales volume were higher than the same period last yera, but it did not reflect the firm's net profit performance," Koestoro told Reuters.
He declined to give further details but said the first half net profit was unlikely to be encouraging. The results are likely to be announced next week.
Koestoro said the pre-commercial sales would help lower projects costs, but would not be reflected in the firm's consolidated sales.
Gresik also said it sold 962,090 tonnes of cement in June 1997 against 727,197 tonnes in June last year.
